EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces a severe escalation following widespread direct military exchanges between the United States and Iran. The U.S. launched over 80 strikes against military targets in southern Iran in response to Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to claim retaliatory strikes on U.S. military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait. U.S. President Trump declared the ceasefire agreement with Iran "over," raising immediate concerns of a wider regional conflict.

IRAN
The United States conducted over 80 strikes against military targets in southern Iran on 08 July 2026, including air defense systems, coastal surveillance, surface-to-air missile batteries, anti-ship cruise missile sites, drone launch sites, and port facilities. Targeted locations included Bandar Abbas, Sirik, Qeshm, Bushehr (targeting an aviation and space facility, an IRGC base, and an air force base vicinity), Bandar Imam, Mahshahr, Hamidiyeh, Dashti, and Choghadak. Iranian sources reported at least one Basij fighter killed in Mahshahr by drone shrapnel, one person injured and three treated in Sirik, and one killed and two injured in Khuzestan (Mahshahr, Bandar Imam, Hamidiyeh). An IRGC member, Mohammad Reza Khazini, was reportedly martyred in Mahshahr. The floating pier in Sirik sustained serious damage, and fishing boats in Bandar Abbas were reportedly destroyed. Iran's IRGC claimed to have shot down a U.S. MQ-9 drone over Khormoj and launched retaliatory strikes against 85 U.S. military targets in Bahrain (Port Salman, Fifth Fleet zone, Sheikh Isa Air Base) and Kuwait (Ali Al-Salem Air Base) using missiles and drones.

President Pezeshkian condemned the U.S. actions, shortening his visit to Iraq for the funeral of Ayatollah Khamenei. Parliament Speaker Qalibaf declared the "era of bullying is over" and listed U.S. actions as violations of the MoU. Rear Admiral Sayyari of the Iran Army warned that Iran's coasts would become "hell" for any invading force, and the Khatam al-Anbiya Headquarters stated that any entity supporting U.S. aggression would be a legitimate target. Economically, the price of oil jumped over 5% to between $77.40 and $78 per barrel, and global stock markets, including Tel Aviv, experienced sharp declines following the escalation. The U.S. also revoked Iran's oil production and sales sanctions waiver.

ISRAEL
The Israeli military announced the elimination of Mohammed Emad Alrahman Abu Taima, a Hamas Nukhba cell commander who participated in the 07 October 2023 attack on Kibbutz Nirim. Additionally, Ahmad Yahya Ibrahim Batsh, another Nukhba commander, was killed in northern Gaza, and Hamouda Abu Daqa, an intelligence commander, was eliminated in southern Gaza in recent strikes. In Lebanon, an Oketz canine unit dog was killed by a Hezbollah gunman in Bint Jbeil, who was subsequently eliminated by IDF forces. No Israeli soldiers were injured in this incident. IDF forces operating in the security zone in southern Lebanon also located weapons in a civilian home in Talusa. In the West Bank, IDF forces responded to gunfire in Kiryat Arba and Hebron, where a bullet hit a house in Kiryat Arba. A military drill is scheduled for 09 July 2026 in the Golan Heights.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu requested a delay in a meeting concerning primaries. Discussions around the "Basic Law on Torah Study" revealed coalition tensions, with Likud considering reservations if ultra-Orthodox parties like Gafni, who oppose any changes to the current draft, do not compromise. Attorney General Yariv Levin publicly called to disregard a Supreme Court ruling, drawing strong criticism from former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eizenkot. A new Zionist political force, "Yisodot Israel," was launched by Hili Tropper and Yoaz Hendel, with Shira Shapira and Elisaf Peretz joining, and Tropper calling for Netanyahu's resignation. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth canceled his planned visit to Israel amidst regional tensions. The European aviation agency removed Israel from its travel warning documents.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces eliminated Mohammed Emad Alrahman Abu Taima, a Hamas Nukhba commander who raided Kibbutz Nirim on 07 October 2023, in an airstrike in southern Gaza. Also killed were Ahmad Yahya Ibrahim Batsh, a Nukhba commander in northern Gaza, and Hamouda Abu Daqa, a commander in Hamas's military intelligence division, in southern Gaza. An attempt to smuggle thousands of cigarettes hidden within pineapples into the Gaza Strip was thwarted by Israeli authorities, leading to the immediate freezing of the humanitarian aid permit for the involved company. IDF forces are currently operating in Hebron and Kiryat Arba in the West Bank following reports of gunfire.

LEBANON
An IDF Oketz canine unit dog was killed on 07 July 2026 by a Hezbollah gunman in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon. The gunman had opened fire on Israeli forces who were scanning a building in the area, and was subsequently killed by the dog's handler. No Israeli soldiers were injured. IDF forces of the 769th Brigade operating in the security zone in southern Lebanon located weapons in a civilian home in Talusa. Iran's Foreign Ministry and Iranian lead negotiator Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf asserted that Israeli strikes in Lebanon constitute a violation of the Iran-U.S. memorandum of understanding.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The funeral procession for Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei is ongoing in the holy cities of Najaf and Karbala in Iraq, drawing millions of mourners. Prominent Iraqi figures, including Muqtada al-Sadr, Ammar Al-Hakeem, and sons of Grand Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani (though Sistani himself declined to pray over the coffin), participated in the ceremonies. Sheikh Zakzaky, leader of the Islamic Movement in Nigeria, also attended. Iraq's Minister of Communications announced the issuance of a special postage stamp to commemorate the event. Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa arrived in Ankara for the NATO summit, where he is scheduled to meet with U.S. President Trump.

GULF STATES
The region experienced significant escalation and responses. Kuwait announced it intercepted two ballistic missiles and 13 UAVs launched from Iran, reporting no damage or casualties, though its Electricity Ministry stated some power transmission lines were disconnected due to shrapnel. Kuwait's Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned the Iranian attacks, stating its security and sovereignty are "red lines." Bahrain's air defense systems were activated multiple times, with reports of new missile attacks. The IRGC claimed to have struck U.S. military assembly points at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain and Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait.

Saudi shipping company Bahri confirmed its oil tanker, Wedyan, was involved in an incident in the Strait of Hormuz, but reported the vessel was seaworthy and its crew safe. Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned attacks in Bahrain and Kuwait, and on Saudi and Qatari commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar summoned the Iranian Deputy Ambassador and filed a complaint regarding an attack on a Qatari tanker, demanding an immediate halt to actions affecting regional security and freedom of navigation. Oman's Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the military attacks and called for all parties to exercise restraint and de-escalation, emphasizing that military escalation threatens regional security and maritime safety. A senior advisor to the UAE stated that Iranian attacks indicate Tehran's inability to de-escalate and that Gulf states will not remain targets. The UAE is reportedly planning to develop new ports, pipelines, and transit systems to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) reported that 6,000 sailors remain in the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  On 08 July 2026, the United States launched over 80 airstrikes against military targets in southern Iran, including air defense, coastal surveillance, missile sites, and port facilities across areas such as Bandar Abbas, Sirik, Qeshm, Bushehr, and Khuzestan.
2.  Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed to have retaliated by striking 85 U.S. military targets in Bahrain (Port Salman, Fifth Fleet zone, Sheikh Isa Air Base) and Kuwait (Ali Al-Salem Air Base) with missiles and drones, and downed a U.S. MQ-9 drone over Khormoj.
3.  Kuwait intercepted 2 ballistic missiles and 13 UAVs launched from Iran, resulting in power line damage from shrapnel. Bahrain also activated its air defense systems multiple times.
4.  U.S. President Donald Trump declared the Iran-U.S. ceasefire Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) "over" and revoked Iran's sanctions waiver for oil production and sales, citing Iranian attacks on commercial shipping.
5.  Multiple commercial ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, including Saudi tanker Wedyan and a Qatari tanker. Qatar summoned Iran's Deputy Ambassador to issue a formal protest.
6.  Millions of mourners gathered in Najaf and Karbala, Iraq, for the funeral procession of Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, attended by high-ranking Iraqi religious and political figures.
7.  Israel eliminated three key Hamas commanders in Gaza: Mohammed Emad Alrahman Abu Taima (Nukhba cell commander from 07 October attack), Ahmad Yahya Ibrahim Batsh (Nukhba cell commander), and Hamouda Abu Daqa (military intelligence commander).
8.  A Hezbollah gunman killed an IDF Oketz canine unit dog in Bint Jbeil, Lebanon, before being killed by IDF forces.
9.  U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth canceled his planned visit to Israel amid the escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high following direct military exchanges between the U.S. and Iran, and President Trump's declaration that the ceasefire is "over." Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where commercial shipping attacks have led to a U.S. revocation of oil sanctions waivers and a potential naval blockade, and direct strikes by both the U.S. on southern Iran and the IRGC on U.S. bases in Gulf States. Southern Lebanon remains a flashpoint with ongoing IDF-Hezbollah confrontations. The U.S. military posture has intensified with extensive strikes and readiness for a potential blockade, while Iran has vowed a "crushing response" and declared U.S. bases in the region as legitimate targets. Iran's red lines include aggression against its sovereignty and territory, and any support for U.S. actions from Gulf states, while Kuwait and Bahrain view their sovereignty and security as "red lines" against Iranian attacks.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The U.S. launched extensive strikes on Iran, revoked oil sanctions waivers, and President Trump declared the ceasefire "over," using strong rhetoric against Iranian leadership. U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth canceled his visit to Israel. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte publicly supported the U.S. strikes, describing them as "absolutely necessary" and a "very strong response" to Iran's ceasefire violations. Turkish President Erdogan praised Trump's firm stance on Iran and expressed gratitude for air defense aid from several NATO members during the conflict, while discussing potential F-35 sales with Trump.

Gulf states expressed serious concerns: Saudi Arabia reported an incident involving its oil tanker. The UAE condemned Iranian attacks and is planning alternative transit routes to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar condemned the attacks on its tanker and summoned the Iranian Deputy Ambassador for an official complaint, while emphasizing diplomacy. Kuwait condemned Iranian attacks and confirmed interceptions of Iranian projectiles, with its foreign ministry calling sovereignty a "red line." Oman called for de-escalation and restraint from all parties.

In Europe, the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) extended its advisory against flying over Iran and Iraq until 31 August. The Netherlands expressed hope for a diplomatic solution, while the EU's foreign policy chief acknowledged that U.S.-Iran clashes complicate peace talks. China's Foreign Ministry called for adherence to the MoU and resolution of differences through dialogue, stating military means cannot solve problems. Venezuela's President met with an Israeli rescue mission, requesting an extension of their humanitarian aid. Ireland's Parliament voted to ban imports from Israeli settlements.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several unverified claims and potential propaganda indicators warrant attention. A CNN report, cited by some sources, alleged a U.S. strike hit a school in Iran, killing nearly 200 children and adults; this specific target and high casualty figure have not been corroborated by other sources which primarily mentioned military targets. The IDF initially reported a female Oketz dog handler killed a Hezbollah gunman but later stated it was investigating the incident, suggesting potential "good-faith human error" in initial reporting. Contradictory U.S. statements indicate ongoing negotiations with Iran in good faith (per Reuters and a U.S. official) while President Trump publicly declared the ceasefire over. IRGC and CENTCOM claims regarding the number of targets hit in their respective strikes (85 vs. over 80) show a slight discrepancy. Trump's alleged claim of 54,000 deaths in Iran's December protests is a highly inflated and unverified figure.

Propaganda is evident in both Iranian and U.S. narratives. Iranian state media heavily emphasize the "martyred Leader" and "massive" funeral, framing it as a symbol of unity and resistance, while portraying U.S. actions as "aggressive" and "terrorist." U.S. President Trump's use of derogatory language ("sick people," "cancer," "scum") for Iranian leadership is characteristic and likely aims to rally domestic support. Some Iranian channels used intimidating language towards Gulf states, referring to them as "occupied islands of Dilmun" and warning against supporting U.S. actions.

Reporting gaps include limited precise casualty figures from U.S. strikes in Iran, the full extent of damage to Iranian military installations, and independent verification of the effectiveness and specific targets of Iranian retaliatory strikes on U.S. bases in Gulf states. The type and origin of the projectile that hit a third commercial tanker remain unspecified. There is also no official confirmation from Saudi Arabia or Qatar regarding the 85 U.S. military targets claimed by the IRGC to have been hit on their territories.
